reading.body:
CyrusOne Cincinnati (CIN2) publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, making it the third-largest of only eight Ohio data centers with disclosed power figures and 18 percent of the state's disclosed IT load.

The 11 MW across 143,778 square feet is a regional, compliance-oriented facility, not a frontier AI training site. Its PCI DSS, HIPAA, and FISMA certifications point to financial, healthcare, and federal workloads, which require security and uptime more than the 100+ MW campuses now used for large model training.

Ohio's disclosed capacity is thin: only eight of 77 mapped facilities publish power figures, and CIN2 accounts for 18 percent of the 60.4 MW total. That concentration is an artifact of disclosure, not necessarily of actual load, so the state's true data center footprint remains largely unmeasured in public data.

The data does not show any announced expansion or AI-specific buildout at CIN2. It tells us what this one facility publishes today, not what Ohio's grid or power supply can support for future compute.
